name: Async actions
description: Zustand has no special API for async logic — actions can simply be async functions that call set() before and after an awaited operation, such as a fetch call.
notes: Since set() is synchronous and side-effect free, you can call it any number of times before, during, and after an await.

name: Handling async errors
description: Async actions typically wrap the awaited call in try/catch and store an error field in state, so components can render loading/error/success states.

name: persist middleware
description: The persist middleware automatically saves store state to storage (localStorage by default) and rehydrates it on load, keeping state across page refreshes.
parameters: stateCreator — the store creator function. options.name — the storage key. options.storage — optional custom storage adapter.
returns: A wrapped state creator to pass into create().
notes: Use the `partialize` option to persist only specific fields instead of the entire store.

name: devtools middleware
description: The devtools middleware connects a store to the Redux DevTools browser extension, letting you inspect state and action history during development.
parameters: stateCreator — the store creator function. options.name — optional label shown in DevTools.
returns: A wrapped state creator to pass into create().
notes: Named set() calls (set(fn, false, 'increment')) show up as labeled actions in the DevTools timeline.

name: immer middleware
description: The immer middleware lets actions write 'mutating' update logic against a draft state, while immer produces an immutable update under the hood.
parameters: stateCreator — the store creator function, where set() accepts a draft-mutating recipe function.
returns: A wrapped state creator to pass into create().
notes: Useful for deeply nested state where manual spreading becomes verbose; requires the `immer` package as a dependency.

name: Combining middleware
description: Zustand middleware functions can be composed by nesting them around the state creator, applying each one's behavior to the resulting store.
returns: A wrapped state creator with all composed middleware applied.
notes: Order matters — middleware closer to the state creator runs first; check each middleware's docs for recommended ordering.

name: Slice pattern
description: For larger stores, state and actions are split into separate 'slice' creator functions that are combined into one store via create(), keeping each domain's logic in its own module.
notes: All slices share the same set/get, so a single store is still produced — this is an organizational pattern, not multiple stores.

name: subscribeWithSelector middleware
description: Adds an enhanced subscribe() method to the store that accepts a selector and listener, allowing code outside React to react to changes in a specific slice of state.
returns: A wrapped state creator whose store exposes subscribe(selector, listener, options?).
example:
const useStore = create(subscribeWithSelector((set) => ({ count: 0 })));
useStore.subscribe((state) => state.count, (count) => console.log('count changed', count));
notes: Without this middleware, store.subscribe() only fires on any state change and passes the full state, not a selected slice.
